teacherNotes.content: Present the pronunciation/reading rule for: R-Controlled Vowels ("Bossy R": AR, OR, ER, IR, UR). Use the 14 Gabarit fields to clarify rule, system, logic, and exceptions.

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner tries to pronounce 'bird' with short /ɪ/.
💡 Solution: Demonstrate that IR merges into /ɜːr/ with rounded/central tongue.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: R-Controlled Vowels ("Bossy R": AR, OR, ER, IR, UR)
1. Definition: When a vowel is followed by R, the R controls the vowel and changes its sound.
2. Rule: AR = /ɑːr/ (car); OR = /ɔːr/ (for); ER, IR, UR = all merge to /ɜːr/ (her, bird, burn). Unstressed -ar, -or, -er = /ər/ (dollar, doctor, teacher).
3. Why? The rhotic approximant /r/ pulls the preceding vowel backward and centralizes it.
4. How to recognize? Vowel letter immediately followed by R.
5. Common examples: car /kɑːr/, star, for /fɔːr/, sport, her /hɜːr/, bird /bɜːrd/, burn /bɜːrn/, teacher, doctor, dollar
6. Counter-examples: Vowel + double R (carry /kæri/ = short vowel retained).
7. Exceptions: war /wɔːr/ (W changes AR to /ɔːr/); word /wɜːrd/ (W changes OR to /ɜːr/).
8. Common mistakes: Trying to pronounce ER, IR, UR with three different vowel sounds.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: ER, IR, UR ALL SOUND THE SAME (/ɜːr/)! Bossy R takes over the vowel!
10. Key vocabulary: r-controlled, bossy r, rhoticity, merged vowel, schwa+r
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟡 A2
13. Associated Visual: 🤠 Bossy R wearing a cowboy hat directing the vowels.
14. Key Takeaway: AR=/ɑːr/, OR=/ɔːr/, ER/IR/UR=/ɜːr/!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Do ER, IR, and UR make different sounds in 'her', 'bird', and 'burn'? (No, they all make the same /ɜːr/ sound)
CCQ 2: How is 'ar' pronounced in 'car'? (/ɑːr/)
CCQ 3: What sound does 'or' make in 'doctor' when unstressed? (/ər/ schwa+r)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Group these words by their R-controlled vowel sound:
🎯 Item: her / bird / burn ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: All same sound /ɜːr/
🎯 Item: car / star ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /ɑːr/
🎯 Item: for / sport ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /ɔːr/
